summary: Outputs Kinect Azure or compatible Orbbec body-tracking joint data, rotations, confidence, and optional IMU channels using a Kinect Azure TOP connection.
key_concepts: Uses a Kinect Azure TOP connection to output body-tracking joint positions, rotations, confidence, and optional IMU data.
The source TOP configures the camera; body tracking cannot be planned from the CHOP alone.
Max Players determines how many skeleton channel sets are emitted, with missing detected bodies zeroing the extra channels.
World, color-image, and depth-image position toggles choose whether joint data is emitted in meters or image-space coordinates.
Body tracking data can lag image data by multiple frames; the docs point to Sync Body Tracking To Image on the primary TOP when synchronization matters.

key_params.name: top
key_params.note: Kinect Azure TOP connected to the camera

key_params.name: maxplayers
key_params.note: Number of player skeletons to track

key_params.name: relbonerotations
key_params.note: Output bone rotations relative to each parent

key_params.name: imuchans
key_params.note: Output acceleration and rotation IMU channels

common_gotchas: Official docs list this operator as Windows 10 April 2018 or newer only.
A Kinect Azure TOP must connect to and configure the camera; the CHOP alone cannot open the device.
Not every Kinect Azure TOP configuration supports body tracking, such as Passive IR depth mode.
Body tracking can lag multiple frames behind image data; use the TOP sync option if tighter synchronization matters.
Only one hardware type can use body tracking in a project at a time; the first cooked Microsoft or Orbbec node wins.
Extra player channels are zeroed when fewer bodies are detected than Max Players.
